heading.loadgistic-title: Loadgistic capacity sharing and shipment visibility illustration
meta.001: MarketVision connects African markets through platforms for business discovery, logistics conversations and transport visibility.
meta.002: Interlocking cobalt and metal frames representing connection and visibility
copy.007: We build technology that makes businesses easier to find, transport easier to arrange and operations easier to see.
copy.017: Connected African markets where businesses are easier to discover, the right services are within reach, and useful information supports everyday decisions.
copy.018: We build platforms for product discovery, logistics conversations and transport visibility. They help buyers, suppliers and transport providers find one another and act on better information.
access.004: Illustration of a business showroom, product collections and direct enquiry
copy.021: An editorial illustration of a business showroom, with three geometric objects arranged as collections and a direct enquiry panel. It is a conceptual illustration, not a product screenshot.
copy.028: Farms, factories and artisans bring their businesses and products into one place. Buyers explore supplier showrooms, build product enquiries and discuss small or bulk purchases directly with the business.
access.006: Illustration of available transport capacity, a shared route and shipment updates
copy.035: A freight vehicle with available cargo space connects to a private network, then to a shipment update card. Precise route lines and a lock symbol convey controlled sharing and shipment visibility without depicting real locations or shipment data. This is a conceptual illustration, not a product screenshot.
copy.040: Transporters share available vehicle space and routes with selected customers or the public market. Shippers and brokers can find capacity, keep trusted providers in view and follow agreed shipments through private updates.
copy.046: We apply the same understanding of commerce, logistics and operational data to consulting and software development for other businesses.
copy.047: We study how work is done, identify where information is missing and define the technology needed to address it.
copy.048: Supplier showrooms, product catalogues and enquiry workflows that help customers discover a business and start a purchase conversation.
copy.049: Tools for provider communication, vehicle capacity, fleet coordination and controlled shipment updates.
copy.050: Systems that make vehicle and device data useful for everyday operations, with clear information about its source and freshness.
copy.052: We start with how people find a product, agree a shipment and share information as work moves forward. Each platform addresses a practical need within that wider picture.
copy.054: Understand who needs which information, how they get it today and where connections break down.
copy.055: Define the users, permissions and workflows before choosing the technology.
copy.056: Build around real tasks, review how the product is used and improve the connections that matter.
copy.057: Talk to us about our platforms, bringing logistics conversations to your website, or building software for your business.

purpose.context: A product needs a buyer. A shipment needs a provider. The people moving it need a clear view of capacity and progress. Better information connects each part of that journey.
portfolio.intro: AfricMade makes suppliers and products visible. CargoChatter brings logistics conversations into the platforms customers use. Loadgistic makes vehicle capacity and shipment progress easier to see.
portfolio.cargochatterBody: CargoChatter adds provider profiles and live logistics chat to websites and apps. Customers can discuss a parcel or a full load and request a quote from providers the platform owner chooses.
portfolio.cargochatterConnection: On AfricMade, it connects product discovery with a conversation about delivery. Other marketplaces and business applications can offer the same access to logistics providers.
portfolio.cargochatterAlt: Conceptual illustration of a logistics provider profile and a shipment conversation embedded in a website
